summary: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a general binary tree.
mainInsight: Search both subtrees: a call returns a node if it is p or q or if a target was found below it. A node that receives non-null results from BOTH sides is the LCA; otherwise pass up whichever side found something.

approaches.name: Store parent pointers + ancestor set
approaches.summary: Build parents, collect p's ancestors, walk up from q.

approaches.name: Postorder recursion
approaches.summary: Return root if root is p or q; combine left and right results.

promptVariants: How do you detect the LCA in a recursive search?
What does the function return from each call?
options: The node where p and q fall in different subtrees (or is one of them)
The deepest node that is visited during the whole search
The root always, whatever the positions of p and q
The node with the smallest value among both subtrees' nodes
cards.answer: The node where p and q fall in different subtrees (or is one of them)
cards.explanation: If left and right searches both return non-null, p and q are on different sides of this node.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The root always, whatever the positions: Only if they diverge at the root.

promptVariants: Why return the node itself when `root == p or root == q`?
What if the other target is below it?
cards.answer: If the current node is p or q, then either the other target is below it (so this node is the LCA) or elsewhere (then this node is reported upward and the true LCA is higher). Returning the node immediately without searching below is correct because the problem guarantees both nodes exist.
keyPoints: A node is its own ancestor
cards.explanation: Without the guarantee you would need to verify both were found.
In the worst case every node is visited once.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Recursion stack space: ___
Explain `if left and right: return root` and `return left or right`.
What do the two lines mean?
cards.code:
left = self.lowestCommonAncestor(root.left, p, q)
right = self.lowestCommonAncestor(root.right, p, q)
if left and right:
    return root
return left or right
cards.answer: Non-null results from both sides mean p and q were found in different subtrees, so this node is the lowest common ancestor. If only one side found something (or neither), that result is passed up unchanged: it is either the LCA found deeper or one of the targets awaiting its partner.
keyPoints: Otherwise pass up the non-null one
cards.explanation: None propagates when neither target is below.

promptVariants: What is the LCA of nodes 5 and 6 in [1,2,3,4,5,6,7]?
cards.explanation: 5 lies below 2 and 6 lies below 3, so their paths first meet at the root 1.

incorrectOptionExplanations.2: 2 is an ancestor of 5 only; 6 is on the other side.
incorrectOptionExplanations.3: 3 is an ancestor of 6 only; 5 is on the other side.
incorrectOptionExplanations.5: 5 is one of the nodes, but 6 is not below it.
